locales.description: Both lists may be empty. Authoring source strings before committing to any target language is a normal state, and check still validates the source.

required.description: A missing string here fails check. These are the languages you have committed to shipping.

optional.description: A missing string here warns and falls back at runtime. This is what lets a language ship gradually without blocking the build.

fallback.description: Explicit ordered fallback chain per locale, e.g. "pt-BR": ["pt-BR", "pt", "en"]. Never inferred: whether Brazilian Portuguese falls back to European Portuguese is a project decision, not a fact about the language.

handoff.description: Where `i18n handoff` writes translation briefs for an agent to fill in, and where `i18n ingest` reads the answers back. Working files rather than a deliverable, so they are safe to gitignore.

targets.description: Export targets. The key is the target name used in a message's targets array.

committed.description: When true, check asserts that committed generated output matches a fresh export, catching a merge that updated the catalog but not the artifacts.

zeroCase.description: How 'no items' is expressed. 'separate-key' keeps it out of the plural entirely, which every target can represent. 'exact-match' permits =0, which Android and Apple cannot express and which therefore fails export for those targets.

placeholderExamples.description: Examples are the likeliest place for real personal data to leak into a provider request. Set to forbidden if that risk is unacceptable.

expansionBudget.description: Warning threshold as a ratio of source display width, keyed by source length bucket. Defaults slide from 3.0 for very short strings to 1.3 for long ones, because short strings legitimately expand far more.

localeExpansionOverride.description: Per-locale multiplier for languages that reliably run long, e.g. { "de": 1.2 }.

severity.description: Per-rule overrides, keyed by rule code. A project may RAISE a warning to an error. Lowering an error is rejected by the loader: the error list is the set of things that break at runtime or ship visibly wrong text.

provider.description: Used only by the translate package. The core CLI never reads it.

dataRetentionAcknowledged.description: Must be true before the first network run. Catalog text is sent to a third party; entries marked sensitive are excluded.

source.description: Where the source strings come from, and who owns them.

mode.description: sync: the platform file stays the source of truth and only translations are generated. adopt: the catalog is the source of truth and export writes the source file too. Defaults to sync when source.from is set, adopt otherwise.

from.description: Platform string files to import. One namespace each.

importer.description: Stated rather than guessed: a .json file could be a Chrome messages.json or a plain ICU catalog, and reading one as the other produces a catalog of nonsense.

path.description: Relative to the project root, or absolute.

namespace.description: The catalog file this import writes. Two entries must not share one.

localeMap.description: BCP 47 tag to the platform's own tag. Explicit and never inferred: silently dropping a script subtag breaks Chinese and Serbian. A locale with no mapping, where the target needs one, is an error.

options.description: Adapter-specific. Android takes localeFormat (bcp47 or legacy) and resourcePrefix. Chrome takes pluralStrategy (explode or icu-runtime).

capabilities.description: The ICU subset this target’s own formatter really supports, for a project with a hand-written translator rather than a stock platform runtime. Narrowing only: claiming a flag the adapter cannot express is a config error.
